memory_update.text: COLD is a direct public-market cold-chain infrastructure candidate for grocery/staples replenishment; verify occupancy, throughput, fixed-commitment contracts, retail solutions revenue, and services margin before promoting beyond Layer 1.

TRAK is a micro-cap speculative exception with unusually pure exposure to FSMA 204 food traceability; survival depends on proof that supplier additions convert into durable recurring revenue and retailer-mandated network effects.

SPSC belongs in the second-order digital-infrastructure lane for retail/grocery EDI and replenishment workflows; verify grocery/distributor mix and resilience of recurring revenue under supplier IT-spend slowdowns.

UNFI is a physical grocery distribution and route-density candidate; hidden value would need to show up in service levels, utilization, supplier services, traceability readiness, margin recovery, and reduced customer-concentration risk.

Next Layer 1C search should map packaging, RFID/labeling, temperature-monitoring hardware, food testing/certification, and private-label grocery suppliers; candidates to verify may include PI, ZBRA, AVY, NEOG, MLAB, and niche packaging names.

node: Grocery, staples, cold-chain, inventory replenishment, and food traceability infrastructure
summary: Expanded the underfollowed lane around grocery/staples infrastructure into four US-listed candidates spanning cold-storage REIT assets, grocery distribution route density, retail EDI/replenishment plumbing, and FSMA 204 traceability software. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. The strongest direct node fits are Americold for temperature-controlled logistics infrastructure and ReposiTrak for traceability/compliance network effects, while SPS Commerce and UNFI represent second-order digital and physical replenishment infrastructure.
